extracted.intended_audience: research funders, funding policy-makers, research administrators, and scholars studying peer review and research funding
extracted.subtask_description: Synthesis of interventions and evidence about what works to improve peer review and decision-making for research funding, describing contexts, mechanisms, outcomes, and unintended consequences to guide funders and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorter applications / limit technical detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortening applications and limiting technical detail (e.g., two-page synopsis, 1200-word proposals, shortened research plans) to focus on research question, methodology, budget, partnerships and potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: two-page synopses, NIH shorter R01 formats, shortened proposals reduced applicant preparation time and increased shortlisted applications. Risks: reviewers sometimes requested slightly longer formats; may require clear guidance on what to include.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer training to improve interrater reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: Training reviewers (self-taught materials or structured training) to explain review criteria and scoring systems, aimed at improving interrater agreement and review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence from randomized trials and pilots suggests reviewer training can improve understanding of scoring and interrater reliability; training can be delivered for novice and experienced reviewers. Consider monitoring for sustained effect and resource needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant training in peer review and grant-writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Funder outreach, grant-writing workshops, and applicant training courses to improve applicants' grant writing skills and understanding of the funding process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Workshops and outreach align proposals with funder mission and have been associated with higher success rates. Educational programmes for students and early researchers provide valuable experience and can increase proposal quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Virtual funding panels and remote review
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacing in-person review with teleconference/virtual panels to reduce administrative cost, reviewer fatigue, and logistical burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies report reduced costs and reviewer burden with comparable reliability in some contexts; barriers include initial investment in technology and higher reviewer rejection rates for virtual panels in some settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced decision models / decision software
rubrics_metrics.description: Use software (e.g., ProGrid, Teamworker) or performance-matrix approaches to evaluate applications, structure discussions, and shorten meeting times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision tools can produce meaningful feedback, streamline discussions and reduce meeting length. Risks: may correlate scores with CV data and unintentionally embed biases; require careful design and validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional submission quotas / limits on resubmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlling application demand via submission quotas per institution, limits on resubmissions per cycle, invitation-only full proposals, and cooling-off periods to reduce funder workload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented by funders (e.g., NSF, NIH) to reduce burden. Unintended consequence: shifting burden to HEIs and applicants (internal review workload) and potentially increasing intra-institutional competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application triage / filter low-chance applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate triage steps to screen out low-probability applications before full peer review to manage demand and focus resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Triage can reduce reviewer workload and allow earlier feedback, but needs transparent criteria and feedback mechanisms to be fair to applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simplify scoring systems (dichotomous scoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use simpler scoring (e.g., dichotomous yes/no or 0/1) instead of multi-point scales to improve reliability and make review decisions clearer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence shows equally reliable but simpler systems can work; useful especially for full proposals. Care needed to ensure nuance isn't lost for complex decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-tier review including public/patient/community involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-tier systems combining expert scientific review and separate review by public/patient/community members to assess relevance, involvement and benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can increase translational and social relevance of funded research; requires training for community reviewers and safeguards to preserve scientific merit. Examples include community engagement frameworks and re-review by trained community representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masking applicant identity / reduce emphasis on track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymize applicants' institutional affiliations and track records or de-emphasize CVs to focus reviewers on the research idea and reduce pedigree bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Masking can encourage funding of innovative ideas and support early-career researchers; potential to reduce anti-innovation and cronyism biases. Practical challenges: full anonymization may be hard and bibliometric cues can still reveal identities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create dedicated funding streams for high-risk/high-reward and early-career researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Design funding schemes specifically targeting high-risk/high-reward research and early-career/new investigators to promote innovation and career progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs (e.g., NIH New Innovator, Early Independence) have increased funding of innovative work and equalised early-career success rates in pilots. Monitor for long-term ecosystem effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote community engagement and assess social relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate criteria and processes that value community engagement, partnership with end-users, and social impact in funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks define engagement assessment (e.g., involvement, priority, benefit). When implemented, funded work showed increased external grants and publications. Ensure scientific rigor is not compromised while adding social relevance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer registries and diversify reviewer pools
rubrics_metrics.description: Create or use registries of reviewers and actively diversify reviewer pools across disciplines, career stage, geography and demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliometrics can inform registries and reveal expertise gaps; diversifying pools can reduce bias and improve match quality. Beware of 'performance bias' if registries favour prolific researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated/semi-automatic reviewer selection using bibliometrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use semi-automatic tools and bibliometric identifiers (e.g., PubMed IDs) to match reviewers to proposals based on expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps targeted selection and rejection of unsuitable reviewers; may improve efficiency but risks perpetuating bibliometric biases and encouraging performance-oriented selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced reviewer-proposal matching algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use algorithms (e.g., network flow theory) and funder guidelines to better match reviewers to proposals and determine numbers needed per proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improved matching can increase review quality; resource constraints and reviewer availability remain limiting factors. Algorithmic matching must consider conflicts of interest and multidisciplinary proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase number of reviewers per proposal / adjust reviewer workload
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign more than two reviewers per proposal and/or allocate multiple proposals per reviewer to improve reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can increase interrater reliability but may cause reviewer fatigue and be unrealistic for smaller funders. Balancing reviewer workload is essential; rotating and ad hoc reviewers can help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant peer review (applicants review each other's proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Involve applicants in reviewing each other's proposals with incentives to provide honest and reliable assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can increase engagement and produce additional assessments; concerns include conflicts of interest and the quality of applicant reviews; incentives and safeguards recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ independent monitoring, conflict of interest policies, reviewer rotation and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Strengthen COI policies, implement independent review monitoring, rotate reviewers regularly, and increase transparency of review practices and reviewer identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims to reduce bias, cronyism and group-think. Transparency can improve accountability but may affect reviewer willingness to participate; balance anonymity and openness appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple independent review panels / interpanel comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ two independent review panels and assess interpanel agreement and impact of decisions to determine reliability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Double-panel approaches can reveal variability and improve decision confidence but increase cost and administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide applicants with early and meaningful feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate feedback summaries (via software) and provide feedback after triage or multiple rounds of online peer feedback to improve proposal quality prior to full review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early feedback improves proposal quality and can increase success rates; tools like ProGrid produced well-received summaries. Timing and clarity of feedback are critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access to peer review (share reviewer comments across reviewers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Make reviewers' comments on proposals accessible to other reviewers (cross-community critique) to enhance transparency and accountability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows reviewers to modify comments and promotes transparency; may change dynamics of review and requires governance on comment use and confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline funding cycles and adjust timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorten review windows, convene committees earlier, extend resubmission deadlines and streamline cycles to allow applicants to address feedback more quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented across NIH to allow faster resubmissions and reduce waiting times; requires coordination of administrative processes and reviewer availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote outreach and publicise funding processes and outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicise submission and success rates, discuss submission policies, and increase outreach to higher education institutions to improve transparency and applicant preparedness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publicising institutional metrics can foster open research culture; outreach (talks, mentoring) helps applicants align with funder priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal peer review and institutional pre-screening
rubrics_metrics.description: Require or encourage internal institutional review/triage and scoring prior to external submission to reduce low-quality submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can reduce funder burden but may shift workload to institutions and increase internal competition; implementation needs institutional capacity and fairness safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of lotteries for allocation (as an alternative)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider lotteries or random allocation for a subset of fundable proposals to address high uncertainty and equalize chances among similar-scoring proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys indicate some acceptability among applicants; ethical and policy considerations remain. Should be transparent and used where merit differences are minimal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Delphi and consensus methods for niche or novel research areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply Delphi processes or structured consensus methods to review novel or niche proposals to enhance deliberation and reduce group-think.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can promote innovation and structured decision-making; resource-intensive and may require careful panel composition and facilitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance use of bibliometrics and altmetrics cautiously
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate bibliometric and altmetric indicators to assess research impact and inform reviewer selection or evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can reveal expertise gaps and inform registries, but metrics can be misleading, discipline-biased, and promote gaming; use as one input among many.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote reviewer rotation and use of ad hoc reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Rotate long-serving reviewers, provide breaks from study sections, and employ ad hoc reviewers to reduce fatigue and bring fresh perspectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported to reduce reviewer fatigue and maintain reliability; requires managing reviewer pipelines and recruiting newer reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support new investigator schemes and pathways to independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement awards/schemes specifically to promote funding of new investigators (e.g., Early Stage Investigator awards, Pathway to Independence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot schemes equalised success rates in some cases and supported career stability; monitor long-term impacts on career progression and research quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance selection/accountability of reviewers with monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Use audits, core principles and monitoring of funder practices to ensure selection and accountability of reviewers align with standards of peer review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Periodic audits and standards (e.g., AMRC audits) help ensure fairness and alignment; requires resources and clear benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider unintended consequences and system-wide impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: When implementing interventions, assess possible unintended consequences (e.g., shifting burden to applicants/HEIs, reviewer fatigue, costs) and effects elsewhere in the peer review ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realist CMOC approach emphasises context-specific outcomes and the need to monitor both short- and long-term impacts; pilot and evaluate before wide implementation.
